title: Offline Reinforcement Learning of High-Quality Behaviors Under Robust Style Alignment
claim: Reaching a target style requires long-horizon sequencing through intermediate styles, so the data must be stitched across them.
layout: 1 row, 5 rendered humanoid poses, left-to-right progression, no text
description: A single horizontal strip of five 3D-rendered, tan wooden-mannequin humanoids on a white background, in a progression from left to right. The first figure lies flat on the ground. The second is crouched and starting to rise. The next three are upright, running with arms bent and legs mid-stride. The poses look progressively faster and more upright, so they read as a sequence from lying down, to standing up, to accelerating, to running. There are no arrows, labels, axes or text inside the image. The eye goes first to the large upright runners on the right, then back along the sequence to the fallen figure on the left. Any annotations about the slow, medium and fast speed styles, or about stitching, appear to be only in the caption.
caption: Long-term decision-making and stitching challenges for style alignment optimization. Achieving movement styles such as high-speed running may require standing up and accelerating, which means navigating through different speed styles and demands long-term decision making. Also, trajectories in D may not cover all the speed styles, calling for trajectory stitching such as (slow →medium) and (medium →fast).
abstract: We study offline reinforcement learning of style-conditioned policies using explicit style supervision via subtrajectory labeling functions. In this setting, aligning style with high task performance is particularly challenging due to distribution shift and inherent conflicts between style and reward. Existing methods, despite introducing numerous definitions of style, often fail to reconcile these objectives effectively. To address these challenges, we propose a unified definition of behavior style and instantiate it into a practical framework. Building on this, we introduce Style-Conditioned Implicit Q-Learning (SCIQL), which leverages offline goal-conditioned RL techniques, such as hindsight relabeling and value learning, and combine it with a new Gated Advantage Weighted Regression mechanism to efficiently optimize task performance while preserving style alignment. Experiments demonstrate that SCIQL achieves superior performance on both objectives compared to prior offline methods. Code, datasets and visuals are available in: https://mathieu-petitbois.github.io/projects/sciql/.
